what: While scrolling a long panel, a pinned video (like a single shot where a product flies in, spins and shatters) is scrubbed by scroll position. Panel progress (-top / (panel height − screen)) is the target time, and the video follows at 8x playback speed (it stops within 0.1s when scrolling stops). In browsers with WebCodecs the whole video is decoded and frames are drawn to a canvas, so rewinding backward doesn’t stutter. The panel below the screen sticks to the panel head (sticky) and covers the screen, and crossing 1024 width swaps the PC and phone videos
ease: none (tied directly to scroll) · catch-up is ScrollyVideo’s playback speed at 8x

options.src: Video URL (mp4 H.264 — the denser the keyframes, the smoother in Safari and file://). If empty, nothing is attached
options.src-narrow: Portrait video for narrow widths and below, default src
options.narrow: Width (px) that splits PC and phone video, default 1024
options.speed: Playback speed multiplier for chasing the target time (ScrollyVideo transitionSpeed), default 8
options.threshold: Stops when within this distance (s) of the target (frameThreshold), default 0.1
options.[data-fx-part=screen]: Direct child of the board — ScrollyVideo puts the video and canvas here and pins them with sticky (as the board’s first child)
options.fx:ready: Event fired on the page when the video becomes playable (canplay — video.readyState ≥ 3, which the original loader waited for). Load errors are also fired, with detail.error.

note: With reduced motion, it stands at the end scene. In an inner scroll panel ([data-fx-scroller]) the same formula is measured from the panel’s scroll instead of the window. Opened via file://, fetch is blocked, so it scrubs by seeking video time instead of WebCodecs (the library’s fallback path)
